meta.title: Operation of Vacuum Pump in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To generate reduced pressure (vacuum) for Buchner funnel filtration, vacuum desiccation, rotary evaporation, and vacuum oven drying of plant extracts and crude drug samples in the Pharmacognosy laboratory.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for all vacuum-requiring operations including rapid filtration of herbal extracts, solvent evaporation, and storage of moisture-sensitive phytochemical isolates.
procedure: Check the oil level in the oil reservoir window before starting — oil should be between the minimum and maximum marks; top up with recommended vacuum pump oil if low.
Inspect the oil for colour and clarity — milky or dark oil indicates contamination; change before use.
Ensure the inlet filter (if fitted) is clean.
Connect the vacuum tubing from the vacuum pump inlet to the apparatus requiring vacuum (Buchner funnel, rotary evaporator, vacuum desiccator, etc.) using appropriate Keck clips or vacuum tubing.
Ensure all connections are tight — vacuum leaks reduce achievable vacuum level.

Place a cold trap (flask immersed in ice/dry ice-acetone) between the apparatus and the pump inlet when working with organic solvents — this prevents solvent vapours from entering and damaging the pump.
Switch on the vacuum pump and allow it to reach operating speed (5–10 seconds).
Monitor the vacuum gauge — operating vacuum should typically reach below 10–15 mbar for a rotary vane pump in good condition.
Perform the desired operation under vacuum (filtration, evaporation, desiccation).
When finished, before switching off: first close the stopcock on the apparatus to isolate the vacuum; then open the bleed valve slowly to admit air and release vacuum gradually.
Switch off the pump only after pressure has equalized — switching off under full vacuum can suck oil backwards into the system.
Disconnect vacuum tubing and clean the cold trap.
Record pump run time, vacuum achieved, and any abnormalities in the equipment logbook.
precautions: Never allow organic solvents to enter the pump directly — always use a cold trap; solvent contamination destroys the pump oil and degrades pump performance.
Always release vacuum gradually before switching off — abrupt venting can cause bumping in flasks and sample loss.
Check and change pump oil regularly (typically every 3–6 months of regular use or when oil appears milky).
Do not use the vacuum pump with corrosive gases (HCl, NH₃, acid vapours) without an acid trap — corrosion destroys the pump internals.
Ensure adequate ventilation near the pump — exhaust gases from the pump outlet must not accumulate.
Keep the pump on a stable, vibration-damping mat.
Do not run the pump with the inlet completely blocked — this causes overheating.
Inspect flexible vacuum tubing regularly for cracks, kinks, or hardening — replace compromised tubing immediately.
